title: 52nd Street and the Three Deuces
summary: Stewart first played 52nd Street with Tatum at the small Three Deuces, which had a well-kept Steinway baby grand and three or four shows a night.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But when you met -- now, you were saying that you met -- you met Oscar Pettiford during those years.
I met him on 52nd Street. That's when

the Street was really jumping. Quite a few groups played on the Street in quite a few clubs, because my stomping ground was the Three Deuces. That was where -- the first time I had played on 52nd Street was with Art Tatum at the Three Deuces.
What kind of a piano did they have at the Three Deuces?
They had a Steinway, baby grand.
They did? Did they keep it tuned?
Oh, that's about (inaudible). They need to resurrect that as an idea for the club owners in New York now.
If it was kept in tune and it was a Steinway baby grand --
How many people did the Three Deuces hold?
Oh, I'd say, oh, about, tops, maybe 50 to 60 maybe. It was small, long place, very small. I think about 50 comfortably.
How many shows did you all play there?
